mainTopic: Whether a פטר חמור is forbidden for benefit before redemption and after עריפה: the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
overview: The amud opens by asking whether the רבנן must hold that touching part of the womb (מקצת רחם) makes a בכור holy, since twin heads would block each other. רב answers that the same kind does not block the same kind (מין במינו אינו חוצץ). The גמרא then asks why the owner sets aside a lamb that he keeps for himself when a donkey bears a male and a female. The answer is that setting it aside removes the prohibition from the donkey, so the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids benefit from an unredeemed פטר חמור, against רבי שמעון. עולא explains each side's logic, and the גמרא defends those explanations against challenges from בכור אדם, רב נחמיה's vegetables, מעשר שני, and שביעית. As an alternative, the dispute is traced to how each תנא reads "שורך" and "צאנך", which depends on whether an animal co-owned with a non-Jew is a בכור. One question on רבי שמעון's reading remains a קשיא. Finally, רבה rules that even רבי שמעון forbids a פטר חמור after its neck is broken, learned from עגלה ערופה. רבא proves this from a ברייתא about טומאת אוכלין, as explained by רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Must the רבנן hold that part of the womb sanctifies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the רבנן must hold מקצת רחם מקדיש, because otherwise twin heads would block each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: let us say they hold that touching part of the womb makes the animal holy. Because if it must touch the whole womb, then even granting that the two cannot come out at exactly the same instant, there is still something blocking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the רבנן of the משנה, who say that when two heads come out together, one of them is a בכור. It tries to prove from this that, in their view, touching only part of the womb is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say אי אפשר לצמצם: one twin certainly came first, so that twin is a בכור. But both heads were pressed together at the opening, so each head blocked part of the womb from the other. If a בכור needs to touch the whole womb, neither twin would qualify, so the רבנן seem forced to say מקצת רחם מקדיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say: introduces a proposed inference that may be rejected
Contact with part of the womb's opening makes the firstborn holy
The entire womb's opening
It is impossible for two events to coincide exactly
An interposition, something blocking direct contact

phrases.english: And the Rabbis — let us say the Rabbis hold
that part of the womb sanctifies?
phrases.notes: Meaning contact with only part of the womb's opening.

phrases.english: For if only the entire womb sanctifies —
granted that it is impossible to be exactly simultaneous,
there is in any event an interposition!
phrases.notes: The other twin's head blocks part of the opening.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the earlier discussion of the twin-heads case to the view of the רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן hold מקצת רחם מקדיש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רבנן's ruling that one twin is a בכור even though the heads emerged pressed together

steps.title: Same kind does not block same kind
steps.stepSummary: רב rejects the proof: a twin's head is the same kind of thing as the other twin, so it is not a blocker.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: something of the same kind does not count as a blocker.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the proof from the previous step. He says there is no real blocking here, so we cannot learn that the רבנן hold מקצת רחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חציצה only counts when something foreign stands in the way. Two fetuses are the same kind (מין במינו), so the other head does not interrupt contact. Each twin is treated as touching the whole womb, and the רבנן can still hold that the whole womb is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A substance together with its own kind
Does not interpose or block

phrases.english: Rav said:
A substance with its own kind does not interpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מִין בְּמִינוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully removes the need to say the רבנן hold מקצת רחם מקדיש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the other twin's head counts as a חציצה. It does not, because מין במינו אינו חוצץ.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, two fetuses do not block each other at the womb, because מין במינו אינו חוצץ.

steps.title: Why set aside a lamb he keeps himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a donkey giving birth to a male and a female and asks why a lamb must be set aside if the owner keeps it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if a donkey gives birth to a male and a female, he sets aside a lamb, and so on. Since the lamb stays his own, why does he need to set it aside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It asks what the point is of setting aside a lamb that the owner keeps for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know whether the male was born first, so the lamb is not given to the כהן (the one who wants to take it must bring proof). If the lamb stays with the owner and nothing changes hands, setting it aside seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: He designates a lamb, used to redeem a firstborn donkey
For himself: the owner keeps it
Why do I need...? A question about why a law is needed

phrases.english: A male and a female — he designates a lamb, etc.
But since it is for himself,
why do I need him to designate it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּלְעַצְמוֹ הוּא, לְמָה לִי לְאַפְרוֹשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה: the donkey case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement to designate a lamb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A designation that keeps the lamb with the owner seems to accomplish nothing.

steps.title: To remove the prohibition from the donkey
steps.stepSummary: Setting aside the lamb removes the prohibition from the possibly-firstborn donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to remove its prohibition from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lamb is set aside to make the donkey permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The donkey might be a פטר חמור, which carries a prohibition. Setting aside the lamb acts as a redemption that lifts this prohibition. That is true even though the lamb itself stays with the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: To uproot or cancel
Its prohibition

phrases.english: In order to remove its prohibition from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפְקוֹעֵי לְאִיסּוּרֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a hidden purpose of the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Designation only matters if something is given to the כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Designation is needed to release the donkey from its prohibition.

steps.title: So an unredeemed firstborn donkey is forbidden — whose view is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that a פטר חמור is forbidden for benefit before redemption, and asks which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems, then, that as long as he has not removed its prohibition, it is forbidden for benefit. Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the answer in step 4. It then sets up the next move by asking which תנא holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a lamb is needed to remove a prohibition, the donkey must be forbidden until then. This is a disputed point, so the גמרא needs to identify the author of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently, it follows that: introduces an inference
Forbidden to derive any benefit
Whose view is our משנה?

phrases.english: Apparently, as long as its prohibition has not been removed,
it is forbidden for benefit.
Whose view is our mishna?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מַפְקַע לְאִיסּוּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה before redemption

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids benefit from a פטר חמור. רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: a firstborn donkey is forbidden for benefit, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: our משנה is רבי יהודה. It supports this with a ברייתא that records the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that an unredeemed פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה. That explains why the lamb must be set aside even though it stays with the owner. According to רבי שמעון, the donkey is permitted anyway, so this reason for setting aside the lamb would not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
A firstborn male donkey
Permits

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught: a firstborn donkey is forbidden for benefit,
and Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds פטר חמור אסור בהנאה
steps.whatToRemember: Requiring a lamb to remove the prohibition shows the משנה holds a פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה. That is רבי יהודה's view, against רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה forbids benefit from a פטר חמור before redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source or logic behind רבי יהודה's ruling that a פטר חמור is forbidden for benefit. This sets up עולא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 we learned that רבי יהודה forbids benefit and רבי שמעון permits it. Now the גמרא wants to know what drives רבי יהודה's stricter view.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the opinion identified in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical basis for רבי יהודה's ban on benefit from an unredeemed פטר חמור.

steps.title: עולא: Something that needs redemption cannot be permitted
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that anything requiring redemption must be forbidden before it is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Is there anything that needs redemption and is still permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives רבי יהודה's reason with a rhetorical question. If something needs to be redeemed, it must be forbidden until then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that redemption only makes sense if it releases a prohibition. So the very need to redeem a פטר חמור shows it is forbidden beforehand.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often reports teachings from ארץ ישראל
Redemption: exchanging a holy item to release it
Permitted (here: for benefit)

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Do you have an item
that requires redemption and is still permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ פְּדִיָּיה וּמוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Anything that needs redemption must be forbidden before redemption.

steps.title: But a firstborn son needs redemption and is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא: a בכור אדם needs redemption, yet no one says benefit from him is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no such thing? A firstborn son needs redemption, and he is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's rule with a clear counterexample, the firstborn son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור אדם must be redeemed with five סלעים, but he is obviously not forbidden for benefit (for example, he may work for his father). So 'needs redemption' does not automatically mean 'forbidden', and עולא's rule as stated is too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: A human firstborn son, redeemed from a כהן
But behold (introduces a counterexample)

phrases.english: And is there not?! But there is a human firstborn
who requires redemption and is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וַהֲרֵי בְּכוֹר אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the general rule stated in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that anything needing redemption is forbidden beforehand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: a בכור אדם needs redemption but is not forbidden.

steps.title: Revised: The Torah insisted on a lamb
steps.stepSummary: עולא's rule is narrowed: an item the Torah insists be redeemed specifically with a שה cannot be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: Is there anything the Torah was strict about, requiring a lamb, and yet it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rephrases עולא's statement to avoid the firstborn-son problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is no longer 'needs redemption' but 'the Torah was strict that it be redeemed with a specific item, a שה.' Such strictness shows the donkey carries a real prohibition that the lamb removes. A בכור אדם has no such specific-item rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah was particular / insistent about it
A lamb or kid

phrases.english: Rather: do you have an item
about which the Torah was particular, requiring a lamb
and it is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה בְּשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 9 by narrowing עולא's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any item needing redemption is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an item the Torah insists be redeemed with a שה is forbidden before redemption.

steps.title: But רב נחמיה redeemed a donkey with vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the Torah is not really strict about a שה, since רב נחמיה redeemed a פטר חמור with vegetables worth its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was the Torah really strict? רב נחמיה son of רב יוסף redeemed it with boiled vegetables worth its value!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new version of עולא's rule with a story of actual practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פטר חמור can be redeemed with vegetables, the Torah is not insisting on a שה. That undermines the 'Torah was strict' argument from step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Boiled vegetables (beets)
At its full value
He redeemed

phrases.english: And was the Torah particular?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: But Rav Neḥemya, son of Rav Yosef,
redeemed it with boiled vegetables worth its value!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי הִקְפִּידָה?! וְהָא רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the revised rule of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the Torah insists on a שה for redeeming a פטר חמור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Practice shows redemption works with other items of equal value, so no strict insistence on a שה exists.

steps.title: The lamb rule applies when it is worth less
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: at full value anything works, but a שה can redeem even when worth less. That special power is what the Torah insisted on.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are not talking about full value. We mean less than full value. This is what he meant: Is there anything the Torah was strict about, removing its prohibition specifically with a lamb, and yet it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies exactly what עולא meant by 'the Torah was strict about a שה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With full value, any item can redeem the donkey, like רב נחמיה's vegetables. But only a שה can redeem it for less than its value. The Torah gave the שה a special power to remove the prohibition, which shows a real prohibition exists. That is רבי יהודה's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Not at its full value (for less)
To remove its prohibition
And this is what he meant

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's reason (via עולא): since the Torah lets only a שה release a פטר חמור even for less than its value, the donkey must be under a real prohibition until then.

phrases.english: We are not speaking of its full value;
when we speak, it is of less than its value,
and this is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: do you have an item about which the Torah was particular
to remove its prohibition with a lamb?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשׇׁוְיוֹ לָא קָאָמְרִינַן, כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן שֶׁלֹּא בְּשׇׁוְיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 11 by distinguishing full-value redemption from below-value redemption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (full value vs. less than value)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah requires a שה in all cases, which רב נחמיה's practice contradicts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any item works at full value. The Torah's special insistence is that a שה removes the prohibition even when worth less.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה lets מעשר שני work for קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the Torah insists מעשר שני be redeemed with minted coins, yet רבי יהודה says קידושין with it works, implying it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is מעשר שני, which the Torah insists be redeemed with a minted coin. Yet we learned: רבי יהודה says if he betrothed with it on purpose, the betrothal is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's logic using another ruling of רבי יהודה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני also has a strict Torah redemption rule: it needs a minted coin. If עולא's logic were right, it should be forbidden for use. But רבי יהודה lets a man betroth a woman with it, which seems to treat it as usable property. So רבי יהודה seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
A minted coin (with a stamped image)
Intentionally
He has betrothed (the קידושין is valid)

phrases.english: But there is tithe,
about which the Torah was particular, requiring a minted coin,
and we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
if intentionally, he has betrothed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי מַעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה בְּכֶסֶף צוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule established in step 12 from רבי יהודה's own ruling elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that a strict Torah redemption requirement proves the item is forbidden, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר שני has a strict redemption rule, yet רבי יהודה validates קידושין with it. This implies it is permitted, which contradicts the logic.

steps.title: קידושין works even with a forbidden item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: for רבי יהודה, קידושין with a פטר חמור would also work. As רבי אלעזר explains, the woman accepts the item for its future benefit, not because it is permitted now.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a פטר חמור she would also be betrothed, like רבי אלעזר. For רבי אלעזר said: The woman knows the מעשר שני is not redeemed by being given to her, and she will go up and eat it in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. Valid קידושין does not prove the item is permitted to use now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman knows the מעשר שני stays holy in her hands, and she values it because she can eat it in ירושלים. Her קידושין rests on that future benefit. In the same way, קידושין with a forbidden פטר חמור could also work. So רבי יהודה's ruling on מעשר שני says nothing against עולא's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: She is betrothed
Becomes redeemed (loses its holiness)
An אמורא whose explanation is cited here

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume valid קידושין means the item is permitted. Here the item stays forbidden. The קידושין works because of the value she will get from it later.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה can forbid benefit from a פטר חמור and still validate קידושין with מעשר שני. קידושין can rest on future value even when the item is currently restricted.

phrases.english: With a firstborn donkey she is also betrothed,
in accordance with Rabbi Elazar,
as Rabbi Elazar said:
a woman knows

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי מִתְחַלֵּל עַל יָדָהּ,
phrases.english: that second tithe is not desacralized through her,
and she goes up and eats it in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר נָמֵי מִיקַּדְּשָׁא, כִּדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 13 by showing that valid קידושין does not prove the item is permitted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the inference (valid קידושין does not imply permitted status)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה validates קידושין with מעשר שני, he must hold it is permitted for benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: קידושין works through future benefit (eating in ירושלים), even though the item remains restricted. The same could apply to a פטר חמור.

steps.title: The woman redeems the donkey cheaply and keeps the difference
steps.stepSummary: Applying רבי אלעזר's idea: the woman knows a פטר חמור is forbidden, plans to redeem it with a שה, and is betrothed with the leftover value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, a woman knows that a פטר חמור is forbidden. She will redeem it with a lamb. She is betrothed with the value left over between the donkey and the lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 14 and applies רבי אלעזר's idea to the case of a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman does not accept the donkey because it is permitted right now. She knows she can redeem it with a שה worth less than the donkey and keep the extra value. That extra value is what makes the קידושין work, so רבי יהודה's ruling does not show that the donkey is permitted before redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male donkey that must be redeemed with a lamb
A prohibition / forbidden status
She redeems
She becomes betrothed
What is in between (the difference in value)

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יהודה, קידושין with a forbidden item can work because of the value it will have later, not because it is permitted now.

phrases.english: Here too,
a woman knows
that a firstborn donkey has a prohibition on it,
and she redeems it with a lamb,
phrases.notes: A lamb is usually worth less than a donkey.

phrases.english: and she is betrothed with that amount in between.
phrases.notes: The difference between the donkey's value and the lamb's value.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, אִשָּׁה יוֹדַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes Step 14's answer by applying רבי אלעזר's reasoning to the פטר חמור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting why the קידושין works (future benefit, not present permission)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה allowing קידושין shows the item is permitted now.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קידושין works through the value difference the woman gains by redeeming the donkey with a cheaper שה.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון holds that a פטר חמור is permitted before it is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון and asks for the source of his view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that one may benefit from a פטר חמור even before redemption. The גמרא wants the logic behind this.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds that a פטר חמור is permitted before redemption
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַאי טַעְמֵאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the קידושין discussion to ask about רבי שמעון's reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical source for רבי שמעון's view that a פטר חמור is permitted before redemption.

steps.title: עולא: the redeemed item cannot be stricter than what redeems it
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains: there is no such thing as an item that is forbidden while the item used to redeem it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Is there anything whose redemption item is permitted while the thing itself is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by giving רבי שמעון's logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שה given to the כהן is fully permitted. עולא argues that if the replacement is permitted, the donkey it replaces must also be permitted. So the donkey is permitted even before redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains רבי שמעון's reason
Its redemption (the item used to redeem it)
Permitted
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'פדיונו' means the item used to redeem (the שה), not the act of redeeming.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Do you have an item
whose redemption is permitted but it itself is forbidden?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: such a thing does not exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁפִּדְיוֹנוֹ מוּתָּר וְהוּא אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the שה used for redemption is permitted, the donkey must be permitted too.

steps.title: Challenge from שביעית produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא: with שביעית produce, the money from selling it seems permitted while the produce itself is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no such case? What about שביעית, where its redemption is permitted but it itself is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on עולא's rule with a case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שביעית produce, after the time of ביעור the produce itself is forbidden. The money received for it seems to be permitted. That looks like exactly what עולא said cannot exist.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there not? (introduces a counter-example)
But look at...
Produce of the Sabbatical Year
The required removal of שביעית produce once it is gone from the fields

phrases.english: And is there not?
But what about the Sabbatical Year produce,
whose redemption is permitted,
but it itself is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וַהֲרֵי שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא's rule from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that a forbidden item cannot have a permitted redemption item.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שביעית produce is a counter-example: the money is permitted and the produce is forbidden.

steps.title: The money of שביעית is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in שביעית the redemption item is also forbidden, since 'the last one is forbidden.'
steps.simpleTranslation: With שביעית too, its redemption is forbidden, as the Master said: the very last one is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by showing that the שביעית case is not a real counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When שביעית produce is exchanged, the item received takes on שביעית status, and each later exchange passes it along. The last item received is forbidden after ביעור, and the original produce stays forbidden too. So the 'redemption' is not permitted, and עולא's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Also / too
The Master said (quoting an established teaching)
The very last item exchanged is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's rule survives: in שביעית the exchanged item is also forbidden, so there is still no case of a permitted redemption item for a forbidden item.

phrases.english: With the Sabbatical Year too, its redemption is forbidden,
as the Master said:
the very last one is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Whatever is received last in a chain of exchanges carries the שביעית status.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבִיעִית נָמֵי פִּדְיוֹנָהּ אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the premise: the redemption item in שביעית is actually forbidden
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The money from שביעית produce is permitted, which would break עולא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exchanged item takes on שביעית status and is forbidden, so the case fits עולא's rule.

steps.title: Another explanation: they disagree about a verse, and here is רבי יהודה's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second explanation of the whole dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון: it comes from how they read a verse. It brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה reads both phrases of the verse as permitting work and shearing of a בכור owned jointly with others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree about this verse. As a ברייתא teaches: "Do not work with the firstborn of your ox" means you may work with one that is yours and also belongs to others. "Do not shear the firstborn of your flock" means you may shear one that is yours and also belongs to others. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of why רבי יהודה forbids and רבי שמעון permits benefit from a פטר חמור before it is redeemed. It starts by quoting רבי יהודה's side of a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of עולא's logical rule, the dispute is now traced to how each תנא reads the words "שורך" (your ox) and "צאנך" (your flock). רבי יהודה reads "your" as "only yours." So an animal partly owned by others, such as a non-Jew, is not covered by the ban on work and shearing.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if you wish, say." This introduces an alternative explanation.
They disagree
As it is taught in a ברייתא
"Do not work with the firstborn of your ox" (דברים טו:יט)
Yours and others'. An animal owned in partnership, here with a non-Jew.

steps.confusionAlert: "Yours and others'" does not mean two separate animals. It means one animal owned jointly by a Jew and someone else.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
disagree about this verse,
as it is taught in a baraita:
"You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox"

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה עוֹבֵד בְּשֶׁלְּךָ וּבְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: but you may work with one that is yours and others',
"Nor shear the firstborn of your flock"

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה גּוֹזֵז שֶׁלְּךָ וְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: but you may shear one that is yours and others',
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּהַאי קְרָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation for both sides of the dispute (steps 7 and 16), as an alternative to עולא's reasoning in steps 8-12 and 17-19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי שמעון permit benefit from a פטר חמור before it is redeemed?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute comes from different readings of the verse. This step presents רבי יהודה's reading.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reading: a firstborn son and a firstborn donkey are excluded
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads "שורך" as excluding a בכור אדם and "צאנך" as excluding a בכור חמור. So one may shear a פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: "Do not work with the firstborn of your ox" means you may work with a human firstborn. "Do not shear the firstborn of your flock" means you may shear a firstborn donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's opposing reading of the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, each phrase excludes a different kind of בכור from the ban on benefit. Shearing a בכור חמור is allowed, which is the source for his view that a פטר חמור is permitted before redemption. רבי יהודה does not read the verse this way, so he forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: A human firstborn son, who must be redeemed (פדיון הבן)
A firstborn donkey (פטר חמור)
Shears (wool or hair)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the textual source for רבי שמעון's leniency about פטר חמור, the issue the sugya has been discussing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox"
but you may work with a human firstborn,
"Do not shear the firstborn of your flock"
but you may shear a firstborn donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכוֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ אֲבָל אַתָּה עוֹבֵד בִּבְכוֹר אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא with רבי שמעון's opposing reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work with a בכור אדם and shearing a בכור חמור are permitted.

steps.title: Why would רבי יהודה need two phrases for the same exclusion?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's reading uses each phrase for something different. רבי יהודה uses both phrases to exclude the same thing, a co-owned animal, which seems repetitive.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי שמעון: that is why two phrases are written. But for רבי יהודה, why do I need two phrases to exclude an animal that is yours and others'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's reading because it makes one phrase seem extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not repeat itself for nothing. Under רבי יהודה, one exclusion should be enough, since work and shearing could be learned from each other. Using two phrases for one teaching is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: "It makes sense." This grants one side before challenging the other.
Two verses, or here two phrases
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Shimon,
that is why two phrases are written,
but according to Rabbi Yehuda,
two phrases to exclude
one that is yours and others', why do I need them?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהודה's reading from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading of both phrases as excluding a co-owned animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition: two phrases teaching the same exclusion leaves one of them without a purpose.

steps.title: Would a human firstborn then be forbidden according to רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: if neither phrase excludes a בכור אדם for רבי יהודה, it would follow that benefit from a firstborn son is forbidden. That is clearly unacceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, according to רבי יהודה, should we say that a human firstborn is also forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another problem with רבי יהודה's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learns from "שורך" that a בכור אדם may be put to work. רבי יהודה used that phrase for something else, so he seems to have no source permitting a firstborn son. That would make it forbidden to benefit from one's own firstborn son's work, which is absurd.

keyTerms.meaning: "And furthermore." This introduces an additional challenge.
Shall we say it is forbidden?

phrases.english: And furthermore, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
shall we say a human firstborn is also forbidden?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בְּכוֹר אָדָם נָמֵי נֵימָא דַּאֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same reading of רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading, which leaves no exclusion for a בכור אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Absurd result: without an exclusion, a firstborn son would be forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: Everyone agrees "your ox" excludes a firstborn son; they argue only about "your flock"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises the picture. Both תנאים use "שורך" to exclude a בכור אדם. The dispute is only over "צאנך".
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that "your ox" comes to exclude a human firstborn. Where they disagree is about "your flock."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges by narrowing the dispute to a single phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יהודה also has a source permitting a בכור אדם, which answers step 23. He uses only "צאנך" for the co-owned animal, so there is no repetition, which answers step 22. רבי שמעון still uses "צאנך" for the בכור חמור.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
To exclude
Where they disagree

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
that "your ox" excludes a human firstborn
is what it comes for,
where they disagree is about "your flock."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא שׁוֹרֶךָ לְמַעוֹטֵי בְּכוֹר אָדָם הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both challenges from steps 22 and 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the dispute: the ברייתא's reading of רבי יהודה is reinterpreted so the disagreement is over one phrase only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה used both phrases for a co-owned animal and had no exclusion for a בכור אדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree "שורך" excludes a בכור אדם. Only "צאנך" is disputed.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה needs "your flock" for a co-owned animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that an animal co-owned with a non-Jew has בכורה status. So he needs "צאנך" to permit shearing and working it. That leaves no source to permit a בכור חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own view, since he says that partnership with a non-Jew is obligated in בכורה. So a verse was needed to permit shearing and working such an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה uses "צאנך" for the partnership case instead of for a firstborn donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a co-owned firstborn really is a בכור, so without a verse it would be forbidden for shearing and work. "צאנך" ("your" flock, not one shared with others) permits it. Because the phrase is used up, רבי יהודה has no source permitting a פטר חמור, while רבי שמעון does.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own established view
Partnership with a non-Jew in owning the animal
Has the obligation of firstborn status
Shearing and work

steps.whatToRemember: In this explanation, the dispute over פטר חמור rests on "צאנך". רבי שמעון reads it as permitting shearing of a בכור חמור. רבי יהודה needs it for an animal co-owned with a non-Jew, because he holds such an animal has בכורה status. Both agree "שורך" permits a בכור אדם.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
as he says:
partnership with a non-Jew is obligated in firstborn status,
and so the verse was needed
to permit shearing and work.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: שׁוּתָּפוּת גּוֹי חַיֶּיבֶת בִּבְכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's use of "צאנך" from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grounding the reading in the תנא's known position elsewhere (לטעמיה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear why רבי יהודה would need "צאנך" for a co-owned animal at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he holds a co-owned animal has בכורה status, a verse is needed to permit shearing and work. So "צאנך" is not available to permit a פטר חמור.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון is free to use the verse for a firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that an animal co-owned with a non-Jew is not a בכור at all. So he needs no verse to permit shearing and working it. That leaves "צֹאנֶךָ" free to permit a פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds that an animal co-owned with a non-Jew is exempt from בכורה. So for shearing and working it, no verse was needed. The verse was needed to teach about a פטר חמור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step by explaining רבי שמעון's side. Because he has no need to permit a co-owned animal, the word "צֹאנֶךָ" is available to teach about the firstborn donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a co-owned animal is a real בכור, so he needs "צֹאנֶךָ" to permit shearing and working it. For רבי שמעון, a co-owned animal is never a בכור in the first place, so it is obviously permitted. The verse is therefore 'free' to teach that one may shear and work a פטר חמור.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal co-owned with a non-Jew
Exempt from firstborn status
Shearing (the wool) and working (the animal)
No verse was needed
A firstborn donkey

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use "שׁוֹרֶךָ" to exclude a בכור אדם. They argue over what "צֹאנֶךָ" excludes. רבי יהודה says a co-owned animal, because for him it is a בכור. רבי שמעון says a פטר חמור, because for him a co-owned animal is never a בכור.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds:
partnership with a non-Jew is exempt from firstborn status,
and regarding shearing and labor
no verse was necessary,
rather, the verse was needed for a firstborn donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 25 by giving רבי שמעון's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying view (whether a co-owned animal is a בכור) explains why each תנא uses "צֹאנֶךָ" differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two תנאים seemed to read the verse in unrelated ways, with רבי יהודה being repetitive.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their readings follow from their dispute about שותפות גוי. Only רבי שמעון has "צֹאנֶךָ" free to permit a פטר חמור.

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון need the word "your" in both words
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, "צֹאנֶךָ" (your flock) is needed to exclude a co-owned animal, and "שׁוֹרֶךָ" just matches its style. For רבי שמעון, plain "ox" and "flock" would be enough, so why say "your"? The question stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי יהודה: that is why "your flock" is written, and "your ox" is written to match "your flock". But for רבי שמעון, why do I need "your ox" and "your flock"? This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's reading. The extra word "your" seems to have no job in his view, and the גמרא admits it has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the word "your" in "צֹאנֶךָ" teaches 'only yours, not co-owned with a non-Jew'. The "your" in "שׁוֹרֶךָ" is just there to match. For רבי שמעון, the exclusions come from the words 'ox' (not a human) and 'flock' (not a donkey) themselves, so the word "your" teaches nothing. The step ends with "קַשְׁיָא", which means the difficulty stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one side)
Because of; to match (stylistically)
Why do I need it?
It is difficult; the question remains unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: "קַשְׁיָא" here is not a full refutation of רבי שמעון's הלכה. It only means this textual question has no answer. רבי שמעון's position still stands.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
this is why "your flock" is written,
phrases.notes: "Your" excludes an animal co-owned with a non-Jew.

phrases.english: and "your ox" is because of "your flock".
phrases.notes: Written that way only to match the style.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Shimon,
why do I need "your ox" and "your flock"?
It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading attributed to רבי שמעון in step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every word in the Torah should teach something. In רבי שמעון's view, the possessive "your" in both words has no purpose.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees a firstborn donkey is forbidden after its neck is broken
steps.stepSummary: רבה teaches that even רבי שמעון, who permits benefit from a living פטר חמור, agrees that after עריפה (breaking its neck) it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רבי שמעון agrees that after the neck is broken, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new point. רבה limits רבי שמעון's leniency: once a פטר חמור that was not redeemed has its neck broken, benefit from it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says a פטר חמור must either be redeemed with a lamb or have its neck broken. רבי שמעון allows benefit from the living donkey. But רבה says that after the neck-breaking, the carcass becomes forbidden even in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (concedes)
Breaking the back of the neck
Forbidden (here: forbidden to benefit from)

phrases.english: Rabba said:
And Rabbi Shimon concedes that after the neck is broken,
it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Forbidden to derive benefit from the carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the textual discussion to a limit on רבי שמעון's lenient ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פטר חמור whose neck was broken is forbidden for benefit, even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What is the source for this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the neck-breaking makes the donkey forbidden. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a living פטר חמור is permitted. So the גמרא wants to know what source changes its status after עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for forbidding a פטר חמור after עריפה.

steps.title: Learned from the heifer whose neck is broken
steps.stepSummary: The rule is learned through a גזירה שוה: the word "עריפה" appears both by פטר חמור and by עגלה ערופה. Just as the עגלה ערופה is forbidden after its neck is broken, so is the פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the shared word "breaking the neck" (עריפה), which appears by פטר חמור and also by עגלה ערופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule comes from a word-link (גזירה שוה) between two places where the Torah uses "עריפה".
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עגלה ערופה (the calf whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder) is forbidden for benefit after its neck is broken. Since the Torah uses the same word for the פטר חמור, the same law applies to it. That is why even רבי שמעון forbids it after עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (derives through a link)
The calf whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder
A derivation from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: A living פטר חמור may be used, according to רבי שמעון. Once its neck is broken, it is forbidden like an עגלה ערופה, through the גזירה שוה of "עריפה".

phrases.english: He derives "breaking the neck" and "breaking the neck"
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה based on the shared word.

phrases.english: from the heifer whose neck is broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר עֲרִיפָה עֲרִיפָה מֵעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of "עריפה" from עגלה ערופה, which is forbidden for benefit after its neck is broken.

steps.title: רבא brings a ברייתא listing forbidden foods
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a proof for רבה's ruling by quoting a ברייתא. The first opinion lists ערלה, כלאי הכרם, שור הנסקל, עגלה ערופה, ציפורי מצורע, פטר חמור, and בשר בחלב, and says all of them can become impure as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? Because a ברייתא teaches: ערלה, כלאי הכרם, an ox meant to be stoned, an עגלה ערופה, the birds of a מצורע, a פטר חמור, and meat cooked with milk can all become impure with the impurity of food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts bringing a source to prove רבה's statement about פטר חמור after עריפה. This step sets up the list. The real proof comes from רבי שמעון's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item in the list is something a Jew may not benefit from, or at least may not eat. The תנא קמא says these still count as 'food' for the laws of impurity. The key detail to notice is that פטר חמור appears on this list.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an opening for bringing a proof)
Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden for benefit
Forbidden mixed plantings in a vineyard
An ox sentenced to stoning (here, slaughtered instead)
The birds used in the purification of a מצורע
The type of ritual impurity that applies to food

phrases.english: Rava said:
From where do I say this?
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Orla, and diverse kinds in a vineyard,
and an ox to be stoned, and a heifer whose neck is broken,
phrases.notes: These refer to cases where the animal was slaughtered instead, so the meat exists.

phrases.aramaic: וְצִיפּוֹרֵי מְצוֹרָע, וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר, וּבָשָׂר בְּחָלָב —
phrases.english: and the birds of a leper, and a firstborn donkey, and meat with milk —
all of them become impure with the impurity of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גזירה שוה reason for רבה's ruling, רבא brings a supporting proof from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא עוקצין) about which forbidden foods can receive טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says none of them are food, except meat with milk
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that none of the listed items can receive טומאת אוכלין. He concedes that בשר בחלב can, because the meat and milk were once fit to become impure before they were cooked together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: none of them become impure as food. But רבי שמעון agrees that meat cooked with milk does become impure as food, since it once had a time when it was fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's disagreement. This is the opinion רבא's proof depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that these items are not 'food' for impurity, and the next step explains that the reason is that they are forbidden for benefit. Since פטר חמור is on his list, he must treat it as forbidden for benefit. Yet he permits benefit from a living one, so the list must mean a פטר חמור after עריפה. That matches רבה's ruling exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes
Since, because
A time when it was fit (here: fit to become impure as food)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read too much into רבי שמעון's concession about בשר בחלב. The text does not base it on the item's status for benefit. The only reason given is שעת הכושר: the meat and the milk were each fit to become impure as food before they were cooked together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
none of them become impure with the impurity of food,
and Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding meat with milk
that it becomes impure with the impurity of food,
since it had a period of fitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן אֵין מִטַּמְּאִין טוּמְאַת אֳוכָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 31 with רבי שמעון's opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's inclusion of פטר חמור among items that are not considered food.

steps.title: The reason: only what you may feed others counts as food
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains רבי שמעון's view from the verse 'מכל האכל אשר יאכל.' Only food you may give to others, such as non-Jews, is called 'food.' Something forbidden for benefit cannot be given to them, so it is not food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The verse says 'Of all the food that may be eaten.' Food that you may feed to others is called food. Food that you may not feed to others is not called food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי שמעון's reasoning. This completes רבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double wording 'האכל אשר יאכל' teaches that 'food' means something that can be fed to anyone, including non-Jews. Giving forbidden food to a non-Jew counts as benefit, so anything forbidden for benefit is not 'food.' Therefore רבי שמעון's list contains only איסורי הנאה. Since פטר חמור appears on it, he must hold it is forbidden for benefit after עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'Of all the food that may be eaten' (ויקרא יא:לד)
To feed it to others (non-Jews)
Is called food

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, only something you may feed to others counts as 'food' for impurity, so איסורי הנאה are not food. Because he lists פטר חמור among them, it must be forbidden for benefit after עריפה. This proves רבה's ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties together two separate areas of הלכה, the laws of טומאת אוכלין and the laws of איסורי הנאה. That link is what allows a ruling about impurity to prove a ruling about benefit.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
As it is written: 'Of all the food that may be eaten,'
food that you are able to feed to others —
is called food;
food that you are not able to feed to others —
is not called food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון excludes the items, showing that his list consists of איסורי הנאה. This completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's reading of ויקרא יא:לד, which defines 'food' as something that may be fed to others.
